𝗕𝗲𝘆𝗼𝗻𝗱 𝗚𝗠𝗣: 𝗨𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗔𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗼𝗿 𝗕𝗼𝗼𝗸𝘀 & 𝗤𝗜𝗕 𝗗𝗲𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝗻 𝗜𝗣𝗢𝘀

📈 𝗘𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘆𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝘁 𝗚𝗠𝗣 𝗯𝗲𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗹𝘆𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗻 𝗜𝗣𝗢. 𝗜 𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗸 𝗮𝘁 𝘀𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗲𝗹𝘀𝗲 𝗳𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁.

One thing I've noticed lately is how many people decide whether to apply for an IPO based almost entirely on its GMP (Grey Market Premium).
“GMP is ₹80 — apply!”
“GMP is only ₹10 — skip!”

But personally, GMP is not the first thing I look at.

One of the few things I check is the Anchor Book.

🏦 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗲𝘅𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗶𝘀 𝗮𝗻 𝗔𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗼𝗿 𝗕𝗼𝗼𝗸?
Anchor Investors are certain institutional investors who are allotted shares in an IPO before the issue opens for subscription to the public.
These can include institutions such as mutual funds, insurance companies and other eligible Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs).
What interests me is not just how much money has come in, but WHO is participating.
I look at:
🔹 Which institutions are participating?
🔹 How much has been allocated to them?
🔹 At what price have they been allotted shares?
For me, this provides useful context before looking at the excitement around the IPO.

📊 𝗧𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝗜 𝘄𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗤𝗜𝗕 𝘀𝘂𝗯𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗶𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻
Another thing I find interesting is the movement in QIB subscription, particularly towards the end of the bidding period.
In some IPOs, you may see something like:
4:00 PM → QIB subscription ~15x
4:30 PM → QIB subscription ~120x
That sudden jump can be fascinating to watch.

But there's an important distinction:
𝗔𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗼𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 ≠ 𝗤𝗜𝗕 𝘀𝘂𝗯𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗶𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻.

The Anchor Book represents institutional investors who were allotted shares before the IPO opened.

QIB subscription, on the other hand, reflects institutional demand during the IPO bidding period.

So when I see a sharp increase in QIB subscription near the end, I don't simply interpret it as “anchors are buying.”
I look at what is actually driving the subscription.

And only then do I look at GMP.
GMP can certainly provide information about market sentiment and expectations. 
But the grey market is unofficial, and GMP can change quickly. 
So my thought process is more like:
Business → Financials → Valuation → Anchor Book → QIB participation → GMP
Rather than:
GMP ↑ → APPLY

An IPO isn't just a listing-day premium.
Ultimately, you're buying a stake in a business.
GMP tells me what the unofficial market may be expecting.
The Anchor Book tells me which institutions participated before the issue opened.
QIB subscription tells me how institutional demand is developing during the issue.

And the financials tell me what I'm actually investing in.
That's why I personally prefer looking beyond GMP.
This is my personal approach to analysing IPOs and is shared for educational purposes, not as investment advice.

#IPO #IPOAnalysis #AnchorBook #GMP #QIB #StockMarket #CapitalMarkets #Investing #Finance #InvestorEducation #IPOInvesting
comment: One additional lens is anchor investor behaviour after listing. Tracking lock-in periods, post-listing holdings, and institutional exits can reveal whether early participation reflected conviction or short-term allocation strategy.
